# Evaluation results (generated; do not edit by hand)

Generated by `backend/tools/eval_edits.py` on 2026-11-17 against **openai/gpt-oss-120b** (reasoning effort low, temperature 0). Cases: `backend/tests/eval/edit_cases.py` (30 cases over the demo DOCX/PPTX/XLSX templates). A case passes only if the **produced file** satisfies every check (target changed, text that should be gone is gone, untouched content survived) - the chat reply is never used as evidence. One run, no cherry-picking: every case is listed below. LLM output is not deterministic, so a re-run can differ by a case or two.

## Performance (same run)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| End-to-end latency p50 / p95 / max | 1.92 s / 56.03 s / 57.63 s |
| Mean LLM calls per request | 1.1 |
| Mean tokens per request (in / out) | 1242 / 108 |
| Total tokens (in / out) | 37272 / 3233 |
| Cost per request (mean) | $0.00025 |
| Cost per edit request (mean) | $0.00031 |
| Total cost of this run | $0.00753 |
| LLM call failures / retries | 6 / 0 |

Cost = tokens x list price ($0.15/1M input, $0.6/1M output, Groq console, checked 2026-11-17). Latency includes the token governor's pacing waits (Groq free tier: 8,000 tokens/min), so it measures this deployment's real behaviour, not the model's raw speed.

Failed model calls report no usage, so a request whose calls all failed shows 0 tokens (the `no_edit` cases below); tokens and cost are therefore a slight undercount.

| no_edit | 2 | 6.11 s | 55.23 s | 30.67 s |

### Model time vs. rate-limit waiting

10 of 30 requests spent more than 1 s waiting in the token governor (total 384 s of the 432 s run). The cases run back to back with no think time, which is the worst case for an 8,000 tokens/min quota; a person typing hits it far less often. Latency with the waits removed:

| | p50 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| as measured (includes waits) | 1.92 s | 56.03 s | 57.63 s |
| model + processing only | 1.41 s | 3.23 s | 3.56 s |

### Where the time goes (all spans from the traces)

| Span | Count | Mean | p95 | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| node:plan | 29 | 14.55 s | 55.62 s | 57.07 s |
| llm:(LLM call) | 33 | 1.28 s | 2.06 s | 2.37 s |
| node:render | 23 | 0.15 s | 0.30 s | 0.33 s |
| node:chat | 3 | 1.18 s | 1.21 s | 1.21 s |
| node:understand | 25 | 0.07 s | 0.16 s | 0.26 s |
| node:route | 30 | 0.04 s | 0.00 s | 1.21 s |
| node:validate | 29 | 0.01 s | 0.01 s | 0.02 s |
| node:respond | 23 | 0.00 s | 0.00 s | 0.00 s |
| node:give_up | 2 | 0.00 s | 0.00 s | 0.00 s |

`node:` spans are LangGraph steps (they include the LLM calls made inside them); `llm:` spans are single model requests; `tool:` spans are search / retrieval calls. Deterministic steps (understand, validate, render, respond) are milliseconds; time is dominated by the model and by rate-limit pacing.

## Run history: first run (before fixes) vs this run

The first run's traces exposed two defects (raw provider error text shown to the user; each retry after a rejected structured call stalled ~50 s because the failed call kept its full token reservation) and one routing miss (an ambiguous request with two candidate files was edited instead of clarified). They were fixed, then everything was re-run. Both runs are single samples of a non-deterministic model.

| Metric | First run | This run |
|---|---|---|
| Task success, all | 97% (29/30) | 100% (30/30) |
| Routing accuracy | 100% (30/30) | 100% (30/30) |
| First-try valid edits | 100% (23/23) | 100% (23/23) |
| Slowest request | 78.66 s | 57.63 s |
| `clarify-two-files` | FAIL, 4 s | PASS, 1 s |
| `impossible-sheet` | PASS, 61 s | PASS, 6 s |

## Failures

None in this run.
